sandbox_note: You have no Orchestra MCP access here, so you cannot call list_pipeline_runs or any other live tool. A fixture file stands in for that data — read it and do the analysis against it directly. Follow the skill's instructions on how to shape the ranked output; don't claim to have called a live tool you don't have access to.

evals.name: top-spenders-default-window
evals.prompt: What's costing the most in Databricks right now? I don't have Orchestra MCP hooked up in this environment, so here's a dump of the last 10 weeks of pipeline run data instead (files/pipeline_runs.json) -- treat 2026-08-02 as the most recent date. Use it to do the analysis.
evals.expected_output: Since no window was given, defaults to roughly the last 30 days (the most recent ~4 weekly snapshots: 2026-07-13 through 2026-08-02), computes a duration x cluster-size cost-proxy per pipeline from the fixture, and returns a ranked table of the top jobs by cost-proxy with % of total spend and trend vs the prior period, followed by 2-3 sentences flagging adhoc_backfill_job's sharp recent jump.
assertions: Scopes the analysis to roughly the last 30 days of the fixture (the most recent ~4 weekly rows per pipeline) rather than the full 10-week history undifferentiated
Computes a cost-proxy from duration_minutes x cluster_node_count (or an equivalent metadata-based formula) per pipeline_name
Ranks nightly_full_refresh at or near the top given its consistently high duration x node count
Returns a ranked table with columns for pipeline/job, cost or cost-proxy, and trend vs the prior period
States explicitly that the figures are a duration-based cost-proxy, not an exact billed dollar amount
Does not recommend specific fixes (e.g. rightsizing, cluster changes) -- points to the cluster-review/job-optimisation skills instead
Follows with a short (2-3 sentence) narrative flagging adhoc_backfill_job's sharp jump on 2026-08-02 relative to its flat prior history

evals.name: weekly-trend-review
evals.prompt: Give me this week's Databricks cost review -- I want to know what's trending up compared to last week. No Orchestra MCP connected here, so use this fixture instead (files/pipeline_runs.json); the most recent row per pipeline (2026-08-02) is this week, and the row before that (2026-07-27) is last week.
evals.expected_output: Scopes the review to the 2026-08-02 vs 2026-07-27 rows, computes each pipeline's trend between those two weeks (up/down/flat with %), and clearly separates nightly_full_refresh (still a top spender, flat week-over-week) from adhoc_backfill_job (newly trending up sharply this week).
assertions: Compares the 2026-08-02 row to the 2026-07-27 row per pipeline rather than averaging across the full 10-week fixture
Reports adhoc_backfill_job's week-over-week jump with a specific percentage or multiple, not just 'up'
Reports nightly_full_refresh as flat/unchanged week-over-week rather than flagging it as trending
Distinguishes jobs that are consistently large spenders (nightly_full_refresh) from jobs newly trending up this week (adhoc_backfill_job)
Computes the cost-proxy from the fixture's duration_minutes and cluster_node_count rather than estimating or inventing figures

evals.name: anomaly-vs-driver-distinction
evals.prompt: One of our jobs is always our biggest Databricks cost -- that's expected. But I have a feeling something else spiked recently. Can you check? No Orchestra MCP here, so use this fixture (files/pipeline_runs.json); 2026-08-02 is the most recent date.
evals.expected_output: Ranks the top spenders and identifies nightly_full_refresh as the expected, consistently-largest job (not anomalous), while separately flagging adhoc_backfill_job's 2026-08-02 jump as the anomaly -- a job whose cost/duration jumped far beyond its own flat 9-week history, not just a top-N-by-rank observation -- and points to the cluster-review/job-optimisation skills for a fix.
assertions: Does not flag nightly_full_refresh as anomalous just because it is a top spender -- its history is flat
Identifies adhoc_backfill_job's 2026-08-02 spike as the anomaly, based on the jump relative to its own flat prior 9 weeks, not just absolute cost rank
Presents the anomaly flag separately from the top-spenders ranking rather than conflating the two
Points to the cluster-review or job-optimisation skills for remediation rather than attempting to fix the anomaly itself
Computes the comparison from the fixture's actual duration_minutes/cluster_node_count history rather than guessing which job spiked

evals.name: no-exact-dbu-cost-available
evals.prompt: Which Databricks jobs are costing us the most? We don't have a Databricks SQL/system-tables integration connected, just Orchestra -- and no MCP access in this environment either, so here's a run-data fixture instead (files/pipeline_runs.json).
evals.expected_output: Falls back to a duration x cluster-size cost-proxy score per pipeline since the fixture has no dollar/billing field and no system-tables integration is available, clearly labels the ranking as a proxy rather than a billed dollar figure, and does not claim to query system.billing.usage or system.billing.list_prices.
assertions: Uses duration_minutes x cluster_node_count (or an equivalent metadata-based proxy) as the ranking basis since the fixture has no dollar/cost field
Clearly labels the figures as a cost-proxy, not an exact billed dollar amount
Does not claim to query system.billing.usage or system.billing.list_prices when the user said that integration isn't connected
Does not fabricate a specific dollar cost figure to fill the gap
Still produces a usable ranked list covering all 10 pipelines present in the fixture, ordered by the proxy score
